A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BlockDialect research. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical descriptions, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments on three LLMs, WikiText2 perplexity, seven commonsense benchmarks, ablations, and synthesized MAC-unit costs.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds model and workload evaluations, NVFP4 comparisons, and hardware measurements of quantization and format-selection overhead.

M1.justification: The 16-dialect formatbook, shared-exponent preprocessing, two-stage activation dialect selection, integer arithmetic, and KV-cache procedure remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of intermediate precision and integer accumulation clarify the existing procedure; additional model tests and hardware implementations do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v4 Appendix F adds MMLU and six GLUE tasks—MRPC, SST-2, RTE, QQP, MNLI, and QNLI—to the retained WikiText2 and seven commonsense benchmarks. This substantially broadens evaluation into knowledge, sentiment, paraphrase, and inference tasks.

E2.justification: v4 adds NVFP4 as an evaluated comparator in Table 9. The original Table 1 comparison methods—MXFP4, LLM-FP4, and QuaRot—remain. The new NxFP discussion is a research-positioning comparison, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendices E–F add OPT-6.7B and models ranging from MobileLLM-125M to Phi-2.7B, with specified block sizes and selected full-path evaluations. They introduce GLUE aggregation and MMLU evaluation protocols. Section 4.3 also adds 130nm hardware experiments targeting 100MHz, including a truncated fixed-point MSE implementation; the original 45nm, 0.5GHz MAC comparison remains.

E4.justification: New hardware analyses test quantization/dequantization overhead and the resource cost of two-stage versus MSE-based selection (Tables 6–7). Profiling and dialect-selection analyses expand to OPT. The SmoothQuant study expands from LLaMA2 to four models, while dropping its separate alpha=0.85 result. Existing block-size, dialect-count, and block-shape analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Averages across tasks and selected layers remain descriptive summaries rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial hardware, OPT, additional-model, GLUE, MMLU, NVFP4, and SmoothQuant results. Existing values also change: Table 1's LLaMA3 MXFP4-32 linear perplexity/accuracy changes from 8.25/68.69 to 8.23/68.31. These are reported numerical revisions, without evidence establishing their cause or a method improvement.

T1.justification: The shared-exponent rule, dialect values, beneficial-range construction, and effective-bitwidth calculations are retained. Additional explanations of normalization and intermediate bit allocation do not introduce new formal assumptions, mathematical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim per-block mixed FP4 representation, efficient two-stage online activation quantization, and hardware-efficient full-path inference. Updated headline accuracy figures emphasize mixed-block configurations already reported in v1; the central claimed contributions and their scope remain the same.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of overhead amortization through activation reuse, the importance of rarely selected dialects for large-magnitude blocks, and NVFP4 scaling costs. SmoothQuant interpretation broadens to modest gains across four models. The block-shape caveat about prefill evaluations not fully representing decoding was already present in v1.

D1.justification: v4 provides a BlockDialect-specific code link instead of only the upstream MX framework link and documents new hardware implementation details, including the 130nm library and 600B register-file estimate. However, it removes explicit module-replacement details and the selected SmoothQuant alpha labels, so documentation is not uniformly more complete.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and new Appendix D substantively position BlockDialect against concurrent NxFP, distinguishing joint versus weight-only quantization, scaling representations, dialect flexibility, and online selection. New model, benchmark, and energy-efficiency references broaden the context, while the generic QAT/PTQ discussion and associated citations are removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively condensed and rewritten. Hardware analysis becomes a separate Section 4.3, SmoothQuant moves into Appendix H, and the appendix organization expands substantially. The title is refined, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: v4 adds hardware-overhead and cross-model/workload tables, expands and rearranges the profiling and dialect-selection figures with OPT panels, and redraws or annotates method figures. The SmoothQuant table is expanded and relocated. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses an important gap in v1's energy-efficiency argument: Tables 6–7 quantify online quantization and selection overhead beyond MAC-unit costs. Broader workload and model evaluations, the NVFP4 comparison, and a project-code link materially strengthen validation and reproducibility. These gains outweigh reduced SmoothQuant parameter disclosure, although hardware evidence remains module-level synthesis and Table 9 shows mixed metric-level wins rather than uniform superiority.
